question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. parliment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "parliment" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "parliament", meaning the supreme law-making body of a country. (संसद)

◦ Correct: The bill was passed by the parliament.

• Spelling key: PAR + LIA + MENT (note the silent "a" after "li").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "perceive" (to become aware of / notice), "pastime" (a hobby / leisure activity) and "perseverance" (persistence / steady effort) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with the tricky "-iament/-ie-" pattern: parliament, friend, believe. Remember the rule "i before e except after c" (perceive, receive, deceive).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The dancer / performed weird / but the music was / highly enchanting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. performed weird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Performed" is a verb, and a verb must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Weird" is an adjective; the adverb form "weirdly" is required. So it should be "performed weirdly".

◦ Correct: The dancer performed weirdly but the music was highly enchanting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The dancer" (subject), "but the music was" (conjunction + subject + verb) and "highly enchanting" (adverb + adjective) are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Adjectives describe nouns (a weird dance); adverbs describe verbs, adjectives or other adverbs (danced weirdly). Most adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
option_2: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
option_3: The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
option_4: The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "dance" is a specific, particular one (defined by the "of" phrase), so it needs the definite article "the" — "The intricate dance". Similarly, "the synaptic cleft" refers to a specific, known structure.

• "plays a crucial role" is the fixed collocation — a role is being introduced generally, so the indefinite article "a" is correct.

◦ Correct: The intricate dance ... in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 wrongly say "plays the crucial role" (should be "a crucial role").

• Options 1 and 2 wrongly begin with "An" instead of "The".

NOTE

• Use "the" for a specific/known noun and "a/an" for a non-specific one. The idiom is "play a role / part in something".

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
option_2: If you want to have an sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
option_3: If you want to have sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
option_4: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "knowledge" is a singular countable phrase here ("a ... knowledge"), so it takes "a" (not "an", because "sound" begins with a consonant sound).

• When "Japanese" refers to the language, no article "the" is used before it — "knowledge of Japanese" (the language), not "of the Japanese".

◦ Correct: ... a sound working knowledge of Japanese ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 wrongly uses "an sound" (should be "a", since "sound" starts with a consonant sound).

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly add "the" before "Japanese" — "the Japanese" would mean the Japanese people, not the language.

NOTE

• Names of languages take no article: "I learn French", "a knowledge of Hindi". "The + language-name + people" (the Japanese) refers to the nation/people.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

RK Laxman was well-known for his drawings of people in such a highly exaggerated manner as to cause laughter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. caricatures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "caricature" is a drawing of a person in which certain features are exaggerated in a comic or grotesque way to cause laughter. This exactly matches "drawings ... in a highly exaggerated manner as to cause laughter". (व्यंग्य-चित्र / कार्टून)

◦ Example: The cartoonist drew a hilarious caricature of the minister.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "articles" (written pieces), Option 2 "sketches" (rough drawings) and Option 3 "portraits" (realistic likenesses) do not carry the sense of comic exaggeration.

NOTE

• RK Laxman was India's most famous cartoonist, creator of "The Common Man" and the daily "You Said It" cartoon in The Times of India.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
option_1: The audience applauded the muzicians performance.
option_2: The audiance applauded the musicans performance.
option_3: The audience applauded the musician's performance.
option_4: The audiance applauded the musician's perfomance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The audience applauded the musician's performance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "audience", "musician's" (with the apostrophe showing possession) and "performance".

◦ Correct: The audience applauded the musician's performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "musicians" as "muzicians"; Option 2 misspells "audience" as "audiance" and drops the apostrophe; Option 4 misspells "audience" and "performance" ("audiance", "perfomance").

NOTE

• "Audience" ends in "-ience"; "performance" keeps the "r" — per-FOR-mance. The possessive of a singular noun adds 's (musician → musician's).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of 'clarify' in the sentence given below.

The last question of the examination paper confused me when it asked to illustrate the Pythagoras' theorem with the help of examples.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Illustrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Clarify" means to make something clear or easier to understand. In the sentence, "illustrate" (to explain/make clear by giving examples) is the closest synonym. (स्पष्ट करना / उदाहरण देकर समझाना)

◦ Example: The teacher illustrated / clarified the rule with examples.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Last", Option 3 "Help" and Option 4 "Confused" do not mean "to make clear".

• "Confused" is in fact the opposite of clarify in this context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of clarify: illustrate, explain, elucidate, simplify, clear up. Antonyms: confuse, obscure, complicate.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Sarvana failed in the examination last week and is in extreme depression these days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. In the doldrums.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in the doldrums" means in a state of low spirits, depression or inactivity; feeling sad and without energy. It fits "in extreme depression". (उदास / निराश अवस्था में)

◦ Example: After losing his job, he was in the doldrums for months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in the red" (in debt / making a loss), Option 2 "in cold blood" (cruelly and deliberately) and Option 4 "in the lurch" (abandoned in a difficult situation) do not mean depressed.

NOTE

• "Doldrums" originally referred to the equatorial ocean belt of calm, windless weather where sailing ships got stuck — hence "stuck / low / dull".

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

Shylock, the Jewish moneylender, and Antonio, the rich Merchant of Venice loathed each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. abhorred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Loathed" means hated or detested intensely. Its closest synonym is "abhorred" (to hate/regard with disgust). (घृणा करना)

◦ Example: They loathed / abhorred each other's company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "admired" is an antonym (to respect / like).

• Option 1 "lathered" (to cover with soap foam) and Option 4 "latte" (a coffee drink) are unrelated distractors.

NOTE

• Synonyms of loathe: abhor, detest, despise, hate. Antonyms: love, adore, admire, cherish. (Shylock and Antonio are characters from Shakespeare's "The Merchant of Venice".)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Head in the clouds
option_4: Thinking about the sky and clouds
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Being impractical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(to have one's) head in the clouds" means being impractical, day-dreaming, out of touch with reality. (अव्यावहारिक होना / कल्पनाओं में खोया रहना)

◦ Example: He will never finish the project — he always has his head in the clouds.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are literal or unrelated meanings and do not capture the figurative sense of being unrealistic/absent-minded.

NOTE

• The opposite idiom is "to have one's feet on the ground" — meaning to be practical and realistic.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Jurisdiction
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Governance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jurisdiction" means the official power or authority to make legal decisions and govern; the range of such authority. Its closest synonym here is "governance" (the act of governing / exercising authority). (अधिकार-क्षेत्र / शासन)

◦ Example: The case falls within the jurisdiction / governance of the High Court.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Expression", Option 3 "Violation" (breaking a rule) and Option 4 "Descent" (going down / ancestry) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of jurisdiction: authority, control, dominion, command, power, sway.

question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.
option_1: Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.
option_2: Sushma is the smart girl of the class.
option_3: Sushma is smarter than any other girls in the class.
option_4: No other girl is as smart as Sushma.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "One of the smartest girls" is a superlative structure meaning she is among the top few (not the single best). Its correct positive degree form uses "Few ... as ... as ...": "Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma."

◦ Superlative: Sushma is one of the smartest girls → Positive: Few girls are as smart as Sushma.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "No other girl is as smart as Sushma" is the positive form of "Sushma is the smartest" (the single best) — a different meaning.

• Option 3 uses "than", which makes it comparative, and has a grammatical error ("any other girls").

NOTE

• Degree change of "one of the tallest": Superlative → one of the tallest; Comparative → taller than many other; Positive → very few are as tall as.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Bindu asked Arya to fill out for / her so that she could / take care of / her sick father.
option_1: Bindu asked Arya to fill out for
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bindu asked Arya to fill out for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended meaning is that Arya should substitute/stand in for Bindu. The correct phrasal verb is "fill in for (someone)" = to take someone's place temporarily. "fill out" means to complete a form and is wrong here.

◦ Correct: Bindu asked Arya to fill in for her so that she could take care of her sick father.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "so that she could", "take care of" and "her sick father" are correct.

NOTE

• "Fill in for" = to substitute for someone. "Fill out / fill in" = to complete a form. "Fill up" = to make something full.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The restaurant's menu featured a variety of __________ dishes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. delicious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "delicious", meaning highly pleasing to taste; very tasty. (स्वादिष्ट)

◦ Correct: The restaurant's menu featured a variety of delicious dishes.

• Spelling key: DE + LI + CIOUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspellings: "delecious", "delicius" and "delitious" are all incorrect.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-cious": delicious, precious, gracious, spacious, suspicious. The sound is "-shus" but spelt "-cious".

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Choose the correct alternative.

She is late than we expected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. later.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "late" is "later" (late – later – latest). So it should be "later than we expected".

◦ Correct: She is later than we expected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "latter" means "the second of two things" (not a comparative of time).

• Option 2 "more late" is wrong — short adjectives take "-er", never "more".

• Option 4 "latest" is the superlative and cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• "Later" (comparative of late — time) vs "latter" (the second of two). "Latest" = most recent; "last" = final.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I always prefer a small, cosy cottage ______ a high-rise apartment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "prefer" takes the preposition "to" when comparing two things: "prefer X to Y". So it should be "prefer a cottage to a high-rise apartment".

◦ Correct: I always prefer a small, cosy cottage to a high-rise apartment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "prefer ... than" is a common error; the correct form is "prefer ... to".

• When followed by verbs, we say "prefer walking to driving" or "prefer to walk rather than drive".

NOTE

• Fixed patterns: prefer A to B, superior/inferior to, senior/junior to, prior to — all take "to", never "than".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

Success demands hard work, diligence and perseverance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Effort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligence" means careful, persistent hard work and steady application/effort. Its closest synonym is "effort" (an earnest attempt / hard work). (परिश्रम / लगन)

◦ Example: With great diligence / effort, she completed the task on time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "indolence" (laziness) is an antonym of diligence.

• Option 2 "Coolness" and Option 3 "Trouble" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diligence: effort, industriousness, application, assiduity, perseverance. Antonyms: laziness, indolence, negligence.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who travels from place to place, especially for work
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Itinerant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "itinerant" is a person who travels from place to place, especially for work (e.g., an itinerant trader or preacher). This exactly matches the definition. (यायावर / घुमंतू कामगार)

◦ Example: The itinerant salesman moved from town to town.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vagrant" (a homeless wanderer with no settled home or work), Option 2 "Nomad" (a member of a community that moves with its herds/seasons) and Option 3 "Pilgrim" (one who travels to a holy place) do not specifically mean travelling "for work".

NOTE

• Related words: nomad (wandering tribe), vagabond/vagrant (aimless wanderer), pilgrim (religious traveller), itinerant (travels for work).

question:
Choose the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully.

His _______________ is a brilliant student.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. son.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a word meaning a male child, which is "son". It fits "His son is a brilliant student." (पुत्र / बेटा)

◦ Correct: His son is a brilliant student.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "sun" is a homophone but means the star at the centre of the solar system — wrong meaning here.

• Options 1 "sune" and 4 "sone" are not valid English words.

NOTE

• Homophones: "son" (male child) vs "sun" (the star). Both sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Woodcutting involves the removal of useless trees first, ________ by medium and finest quality timber trees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. followed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "followed by" means coming after in sequence. Useless trees are removed first, "followed by" medium and finest quality trees — showing the order. (उसके बाद)

◦ Correct: ... removal of useless trees first, followed by medium and finest quality timber trees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "adjusted by", Option 3 "enacted by" and Option 4 "compared by" do not fit the idea of sequence/order.

NOTE

• "Followed by" is used to show what comes next in a series, e.g., the starter, followed by the main course, followed by dessert.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous quotation by P. B. Shelley is "If winter comes, can spring be far behind?" — meaning after hard times, good times surely follow. The fixed word is "behind". (यदि सर्दी आई है, तो वसंत दूर नहीं)

◦ Correct: "If winter comes, can spring be far behind?"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "far" is already present in the sentence ("far ___"), so options adding another "far" (Option 3 "far behind") or extra words ("behind and far", "behind and below") make the phrase redundant or ungrammatical.

NOTE

• This line is the closing line of Shelley's poem "Ode to the West Wind", a message of hope and optimism.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. last.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Last" here is a verb meaning to continue for a period of time. The winter "will not last till perpetuity" means it will not continue forever. (बना रहना / टिकना)

◦ Correct: ... we know that it will not last till perpetuity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hold" and Option 3 "hold on" do not fit the sense of "continue for a duration" with "till perpetuity".

• Option 4 "rest" means to relax, which is illogical here.

NOTE

• "Last" as a verb = to endure/continue (The meeting lasted two hours). "Perpetuity" = a state that lasts forever.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. infuses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Spring" is singular third person, so the verb must take "-s": "Spring infuses a new life in us." "Infuse" means to fill/instil (someone) with a quality or feeling. (भर देना / संचारित करना)

◦ Correct: Spring infuses a new life in us.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "imbue", 2 "immerse" and 3 "inculcate" are all in the base form and do not agree with the singular subject "Spring" (they would need "infuses"-type "-s"). Only "infuses" has correct subject–verb agreement.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject (Spring) takes a singular verb with "-s" (infuses). Synonyms of infuse: instil, imbue, fill, inspire.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. come out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "come out" means to appear / emerge / bloom. Buds "come out as flowers" means the buds open and appear as flowers in spring. (खिलना / निकलना)

◦ Correct: ... buds come out as flowers ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "take out" (to remove), Option 3 "fall over" (to topple) and Option 4 "pull out" (to withdraw) do not fit the blooming of buds.

NOTE

• "Come out" has several meanings: to appear (the sun came out), to be published (the book came out), to bloom (flowers come out).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. suck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Butterflies feed by sucking the sweet nectar from flowers through their long tube-like tongue (proboscis). "suck on the sweet nectar" is the natural expression. (चूसना)

◦ Correct: ... butterflies fly from one flower to another to suck on the sweet nectar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gulp" (to swallow quickly), Option 3 "gobble" (to eat hurriedly, of solid food) and Option 2 "food" (a noun, not a verb) do not correctly describe how butterflies take in liquid nectar.

NOTE

• A butterfly draws up nectar with its proboscis — a coiled, straw-like mouthpart — so "suck" is the apt verb. "Suck on" = to draw liquid by suction.

question: Who among the following led the Indian delegation to attend the 56th Annual General Meeting of the Board of Governors of Asian Development Bank (ADB) along with Investor/ Bilateral and other associated meetings, in Incheon, the Republic of Korea, from 2 to 5 May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nirmala Sitharaman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister of India, led the Indian delegation to the 56th Annual General Meeting of the ADB Board of Governors, held in Incheon, Republic of Korea (2–5 May 2023). (निर्मला सीतारमण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established in 1966 and is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.

• Its aim is to promote social and economic development in Asia and the Pacific; India is a founding member.

NOTE

• Nirmala Sitharaman became India's first full-time woman Finance Minister in 2019. She is also the Ex-officio Chairperson-type representative for India at the ADB and World Bank Governor forums.

question: According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, it is the fundamental duty of every person to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ______________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is integrity of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties. One of them is "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India". (अनुच्छेद 51क — भारत की संप्रभुता, एकता और अखंडता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th (parents to provide education to children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Constitution and were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eutrophication.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eutrophication" is the process by which a water body becomes over-enriched with nutrients (mainly nitrogen and phosphorus), causing excessive algal growth (algal bloom) which depletes the dissolved oxygen and harms aquatic life. (सुपोषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Biomagnification — increase in concentration of a toxic substance (e.g., DDT) as it moves up the food chain.

• Bioaccumulation — gradual build-up of substances in a single organism over time.

• Hypoxia — a condition of low/insufficient oxygen (a consequence of eutrophication).

NOTE

• Eutrophication is largely caused by fertiliser run-off and sewage. The resulting oxygen depletion can create "dead zones" in lakes and coastal waters.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters was associated with the series of nine articles known as 'New Lamp for Old'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurobindo Ghose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aurobindo Ghose (Sri Aurobindo) wrote the series of nine articles titled "New Lamps for Old" (1893–94), published in the Indu Prakash newspaper, criticising the moderate policies of the early Indian National Congress. (अरबिंदो घोष — 'न्यू लैम्प्स फॉर ओल्ड')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Aurobindo was a prominent extremist (Garam Dal) leader who later turned to spirituality and founded the Aurobindo Ashram at Puducherry.

• He was tried in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908).

NOTE

• His major works include "The Life Divine", "Savitri" and "Essays on the Gita". He is remembered as a philosopher, yogi and nationalist.

question: The Buland Darwaza was the structure built by Akbar at which of the following places in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fatehpur Sikri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Buland Darwaza ("Gate of Magnificence") was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh) around 1575–76 to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. (बुलंद दरवाज़ा — फतेहपुर सीकरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of the highest gateways in the world (about 54 metres) and is built of red sandstone with marble inlay.

• Fatehpur Sikri, founded by Akbar, was the Mughal capital for a short period and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Other structures at Fatehpur Sikri: Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

question: Who introduced 'Objective Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the "Objectives Resolution" in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946. It laid down the fundamental ideals and philosophy of the Constitution. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू — उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947 and later formed the basis of the Preamble of the Constitution.

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

NOTE

• The Preamble declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic ("Socialist" and "Secular" were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).

question: Raja and Radha Reddy were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving a new dimension to which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja and Radha Reddy are legendary exponents of the Kuchipudi classical dance form; they were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving it a new dimension. (कुचिपुड़ी — राजा और राधा रेड्डी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi; it combines dance, drama and song.

• A signature element is dancing on the rim of a brass plate (tarangam).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: 'The Best Mistakes of My Life' is an autobiography of which Indian Actor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Best Mistakes of My Life" is the autobiography of the veteran Indian actor Sanjay Khan. (संजय खान की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sanjay Khan is known for films and TV serials such as "The Sword of Tipu Sultan" and "Jai Hanuman".

• He is the brother of actor Feroz Khan.

NOTE

• Notable autobiographies: Dilip Kumar — "The Substance and the Shadow"; Naseeruddin Shah — "And Then One Day"; Rishi Kapoor — "Khullam Khulla".

question: Which of the following options contains groups of cropping seasons in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabi, Kharif and Zaid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has three main cropping seasons: Rabi, Kharif and Zaid. (फ़सल के तीन मौसम — रबी, खरीफ़ और ज़ायद)

◦ Rabi — sown in winter (Oct–Dec), harvested in spring (e.g., wheat, gram, mustard).

◦ Kharif — sown in the monsoon (Jun–Jul), harvested in autumn (e.g., rice, maize, cotton).

◦ Zaid — grown in summer between rabi and kharif (e.g., watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Podu" and "Jhum" are types of shifting cultivation, not cropping seasons.

NOTE

• Major Rabi crops: wheat, barley, peas, gram, mustard. Major Kharif crops: paddy, jowar, bajra, tur, cotton, groundnut.

question: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is plasmodesmata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plasmodesmata" are microscopic channels/tunnels that pass through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells, connecting their cytoplasm and allowing transport and communication. (प्लास्मोडेस्माटा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ribosome — the site of protein synthesis.

• Protoplasm — the living material (cytoplasm + nucleus) of a cell.

• Peroxisome — an organelle involved in breaking down fatty acids and detoxification.

NOTE

• Plasmodesmata are unique to plant cells and are functionally similar to gap junctions in animal cells.

question: Which state topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games, held in Goa (2023), with the highest number of medals. (महाराष्ट्र — 37वें राष्ट्रीय खेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 37th National Games were held in Goa from 25 October to 9 November 2023.

• The mascot was "Moga" (the Indian gaur), Goa's state animal.

NOTE

• The 36th National Games (2022) were held in Gujarat, where Services topped the medal tally, followed by Maharashtra and Haryana.

question: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, who became the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy, is known for playing which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghatam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram (Vikku Vinayakram) is a legendary player of the "Ghatam" — a clay pot percussion instrument of Carnatic music. He was the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy Award. (घटम — विक्कू विनायकरम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Ghatam is one of the oldest percussion instruments of South India, made of clay with a narrow mouth.

• Vinayakram was part of the fusion band "Shakti" (with John McLaughlin and Zakir Hussain) and received the Padma Bhushan and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Other South Indian percussion: Mridangam (double-headed drum), Kanjira (small frame drum), Morsing (jaw harp).

question: During the Mauryan society, Megasthenes divided the Indian society into seven distinct groups. In which distinct group were the 'king's counsellors' placed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seventh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Greek ambassador Megasthenes, in his book "Indica", divided Mauryan society into seven classes. The "councillors and assessors" (king's counsellors) formed the seventh class — the smallest in number but the highest in dignity. (मेगस्थनीज़ — सातवाँ वर्ग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus Nikator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

• The seven classes he described were: philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, magistrates/overseers, and councillors.

NOTE

• The Mauryan Empire (c. 322–185 BCE) was founded by Chandragupta Maurya with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

question: How many other members are there in the Finance Commission EXCEPT, Chairman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four (4) other members appointed by the President. (वित्त आयोग — अध्यक्ष के अलावा 4 सदस्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 280; it is constituted every five years (or earlier).

• Its main task is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States (vertical and horizontal devolution).

NOTE

• The First Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by K. C. Neogy; the 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N. K. Singh. The 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

question: Bhangra and Giddha dance forms are associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhangra" (performed by men) and "Giddha" (performed by women) are the famous folk dances of Punjab, usually performed during the harvest festival of Baisakhi. (भांगड़ा और गिद्दा — पंजाब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhangra is a lively, energetic dance associated with the dhol drum.

• Giddha is known for its boliyan (rhythmic couplets/songs) and graceful movements.

NOTE

• Folk dances: Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Lavani (Maharashtra), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bihu (Assam), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand).

question: Which of the following banking institutions played an instrumental role in financial inclusion through microfinance loans and their expansion in India?
option_4: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) played an instrumental role in financial inclusion by promoting microfinance through the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme and its expansion across rural India. (नाबार्ड — माइक्रोफाइनेंस/वित्तीय समावेशन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NABARD was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee; it is the apex bank for agriculture and rural development.

• It launched the pioneering SHG–Bank Linkage Programme in 1992 to bring the rural poor into formal banking.

NOTE

• Financial inclusion means providing affordable banking services to all; other steps include the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) and Payments Banks.

question: Deodhar Trophy is given in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Deodhar Trophy" is a domestic one-day (List A) cricket tournament in India, named after Prof. D. B. Deodhar, the "Grand Old Man of Indian Cricket". (देवधर ट्रॉफी — क्रिकेट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other domestic cricket trophies: Ranji Trophy (first-class), Duleep Trophy (zonal first-class), Vijay Hazare Trophy (one-day), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20), Irani Trophy.

NOTE

• Trophies of other sports: Hockey — Dhyan Chand Trophy; Football — Durand Cup, Santosh Trophy; Badminton — Thomas Cup, Uber Cup.

question: The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is halogens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are called the "halogens". They include Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I) and Astatine (At). (हैलोजन — समूह 17)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Halogens are highly reactive non-metals; they have 7 electrons in their outermost shell and gain one electron to form –1 ions (halides).

• The word "halogen" means "salt-former".

NOTE

• Group 1 — Alkali metals; Group 2 — Alkaline earth metals; Group 17 — Halogens; Group 18 — Noble (inert) gases.

question: Who among the following married the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and received the title 'Nur Jahan'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mehrunnisa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mehrunnisa married Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and was given the title "Nur Jahan" ("Light of the World"). (मेहरुन्निसा — नूरजहाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nur Jahan was highly influential and virtually ran the administration during Jahangir's later reign; coins were struck in her name.

• She belonged to the powerful "Nur Jahan Junta" and was the daughter of Itmad-ud-Daulah (Mirza Ghiyas Beg).

NOTE

• Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu) was the wife of Shah Jahan, in whose memory the Taj Mahal was built. She was Nur Jahan's niece.

question: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iodine solution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Iodine solution" is used to test for starch. When iodine is added to a food containing starch, it turns blue-black, confirming the presence of starch. (आयोडीन विलयन — स्टार्च परीक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The blue-black colour is due to iodine molecules getting trapped inside the coiled (helical) structure of the starch molecule (amylose).

• Starch is a carbohydrate (polysaccharide) and the main storage food in plants.

NOTE

• Food tests: Starch → iodine (blue-black); Protein → Biuret test (violet); Reducing sugar → Benedict's/Fehling's test (brick-red); Fat → grease-spot / Sudan III.

question: Which of the following ministries has launched the National Career Service Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) ?
option_2: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
option_4: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Labour and Employment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Career Service (NCS) Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to provide job-matching, career counselling and employment-related services. (श्रम एवं रोज़गार मंत्रालय — NCS पोर्टल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NCS portal was launched in 2015; it connects job-seekers, employers, skill providers and career counsellors on a single digital platform.

• It replaced the older employment exchange system with a transparent online mechanism.

NOTE

• Other schemes of the Ministry of Labour and Employment: e-Shram portal (for unorganised workers), EPFO, ESIC, and the four Labour Codes.

question: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories has the highest percentage of rural population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, among the Union Territories, Puducherry had the highest percentage of rural population (about 31.7%). (पुडुचेरी — सर्वाधिक ग्रामीण जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Delhi and Chandigarh are highly urbanised UTs (Delhi ~97.5% urban, Chandigarh ~97.25% urban).

• Overall, India's rural population as per Census 2011 was about 68.84%.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". Himachal Pradesh had the highest rural population percentage among states.

question: On which of the following days is National Integration Day observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19 November.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Integration Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas in this sense / Quami Ekta Diwas) is observed on 19 November, the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. (राष्ट्रीय एकता दिवस — 19 नवंबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The day promotes national unity, peace, and communal harmony.

• Note: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) is separately observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

NOTE

• Important national days: 2 October — Gandhi Jayanti; 15 August — Independence Day; 26 January — Republic Day; 19 November — National Integration Day (Indira Gandhi's birthday).

question: Which of the following is not a tributary of Godavari River?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kameng.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kameng" is NOT a tributary of the Godavari — it is a tributary of the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh. The Godavari's tributaries include Indravati, Pranhita, Manjra, Purna, Wardha and Sabari. (कामेंग — गोदावरी की सहायक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Godavari is the largest river of Peninsular India (the "Dakshin Ganga"); it rises at Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra) and flows into the Bay of Bengal.

• Its total length is about 1,465 km.

NOTE

• Major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari: Purna, Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari; right-bank: Pravara, Manjra, Manair.

question: Who among the following are the target beneficiaries for the 'Vishwakarma Yojana' launched by Government of India on 17 September 2023?
option_1: Individuals skilled in traditional folk dance
option_4: Individuals skilled in traditional folk songs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "PM Vishwakarma Yojana", launched on 17 September 2023 (Vishwakarma Jayanti / PM's birthday), targets individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship — artisans and craftspeople (Vishwakarmas) who work with their hands and tools. (पीएम विश्वकर्मा योजना — पारंपरिक कारीगर/शिल्पकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It covers 18 traditional trades such as carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, cobblers, tailors, barbers, masons, etc.

• Benefits include skill training, a toolkit incentive, collateral-free credit (loans) at concessional interest, and digital/market support.

NOTE

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) to strengthen and support artisan communities.
